articles.title: SpaceX Starship test to attempt first-ever spaceship 'catch'
articles.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking "catch" of the spaceship following a day in orbit.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship conducted a revolutionary test attempting to catch the massive booster with mechanical arms, representing a landmark innovation in reusable rocket technology.

articles.title: A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A groundbreaking new supercomputer simulation is revealing how the universe escaped its cosmic dark age and transformed into a cosmos filled with stars and galaxies. Called Lumina, it recreates 2 billion years of early cosmic history across a region 1.6 billion light-years wide, capturing extraordinary details that previous simulations could not.
articles.summary: A groundbreaking supercomputer simulation demonstrates how the universe emerged from its cosmic dark age to become the luminous cosmos we observe today. This landmark achievement illuminates one of cosmology's greatest mysteries.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
articles.description: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars.  Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: On November 13, 1971, NASA's Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars, revolutionizing our understanding of the Red Planet. This historic milestone laid the foundation for decades of Mars exploration.

articles.title: 900 millions de galaxies : Euclid ouvre un trésor cosmique qui pourrait bouleverser notre vision de l'Univers
articles.description: Après plus d'un an à scruter les profondeurs du cosmos, le télescope spatial Euclid vient de franchir une étape décisive. Les astrophysiciens du monde entier vont pouvoir explorer une quantité vertigineuse de nouvelles données en plus d'une mosaïque d'images …
articles.summary: The Euclid space telescope has catalogued 900 million galaxies after more than a year of observation, potentially transforming our understanding of the universe.

articles.title: PREVIEW: SpaceX's 15th Starship flight to test future of rocket reusability
articles.description: SpaceX is set to conduct its next Starship test flight on Friday, a mission that could mark a turning point in rocket launch operations. The company aims to recover both the Super Heavy booster and th...
articles.summary: SpaceX's 15th Starship test flight aims to achieve a historic dual rocket booster landing, potentially marking a breakthrough moment in reusable rocket technology. This mission could transform the economics of space access.

articles.title: SpaceX Starship Flight 15 live updates: Super Heavy rocket moved to launch pad for 1st Starship double landing test
articles.description: SpaceX is counting down to make history with the launch of its Starship Flight 15 mission on Friday, Nov. 13, with liftoff scheduled for 5:45 p.m. EDT (2245 GMT) at Starbase, Texas. Starship Flight 15 will attempt to land both Starship Ship and Super Heavy Bo…
articles.summary: SpaceX prepares Starship Flight 15's Super Heavy booster for launch, aiming for the first-ever double landing test of orbital-class rocket boosters. This mission represents a watershed moment in rocket reusability technology.

articles.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
articles.description: A breakthrough in telescope imaging could reveal countless alien worlds that have been hiding in plain sight. Scientists developed a new technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove the overwhelming glare of stars, making fai…
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a previously hidden exoplanet using James Webb Space Telescope imaging techniques, suggesting countless alien worlds may be waiting in existing astronomical data. This breakthrough could revolutionize exoplanet discovery methods.

articles.title: LOFAR Takes the Deepest Image of the Low-Frequency Radio Sky to Date
articles.description: Using the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR), an international team led by Leiden University has produced the sharpest and most sensitive radio image of the sky ever made at low radio frequencies.
articles.summary: The LOFAR international observatory has captured the deepest and sharpest low-frequency radio sky image ever taken, advancing our understanding of cosmic radio sources and structure.

articles.title: Dense Galaxy Clusters Foster Mechanisms That Throttle Star Formation
articles.description: The Cosmic Noon was when the Universe's Stelliferous Era Began, and star formation was prodigious during that epoch. But since then, star formation has slowed to a relative crawl, despite the fact that we can watch them forming in regions throughout the Milky Way. What happened to the hydrogen gas that forms stars? New research found clues in a particulary dense galaxy cluster.
articles.summary: Researchers discovered mechanisms within dense galaxy clusters during Cosmic Noon that regulate star formation, revealing how the universe's stellar production evolved across cosmic history.

articles.title: Euclid's First Data Release: A Stepping Stone to its 3D Map of the Sky
articles.description: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope has released its first huge batch of data. It's all part of the telescope's mission to study dark energy and dark matter. The telescope is busy creating the largest ever 3D map of the Universe with its huge 600 megapixel camera, and new images give us some highlights.
articles.summary: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope has released its first major data batch, advancing its ambitious mission to create a comprehensive 3D map of the universe's structure and dark matter distribution.

articles.title: Asteroid Bennu's Sample Delivers Another Surprise
articles.description: Researchers compared the samples from asteroid Bennu with the Murchison meteorite and measured the amino acid β-alanine in both. Using new techniques, they were able to measure not only their isotopic compositions, but isotopic differences between individual atoms in the same molecule. The results show that some of the same pre-cursors to life formed in different conditions and positions in the protoplanetary disk.
articles.summary: Analysis of samples from asteroid Bennu reveals organic compounds including amino acids, providing insights into the building blocks of life present in the early solar system.

articles.title: A likely supermassive neutron star might shed light on the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes
articles.description: A team of astronomers recently identified a red giant star with an unseen binary companion after examining data from the Large Sky Area MultiObject Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE). Although the companion object can't be observed visually, astronomers can see the gravitational effects it has on the red giant star.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers identified a likely supermassive neutron star that may illuminate the mysterious mass gap between neutron stars and black holes, advancing stellar physics understanding.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance confirms a key ingredient for life hidden in ancient Mars rocks
articles.description: NASA's Perseverance rover has confirmed complex organic carbon just beneath the surface of ancient Martian rocks, raising intriguing questions about the Red Planet's potential to have supported life. The remarkable preservation of these compounds, along with similar discoveries thousands of miles away, suggests the building blocks of life may once have been widespread across Mars.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover confirmed the presence of complex organic carbon beneath Martian rock surfaces, strengthening evidence that ancient Mars had conditions favorable for life.

articles.title: Dark energy may have flipped from negative to positive 9.5 billion years ago
articles.description: A mysterious force driving the expansion of the Universe may have undergone a dramatic reversal billions of years ago. Scientists exploring an overlooked branch of an alternative gravity theory discovered that dark energy could have switched from negative to positive roughly 9.5 billion years ago, potentially changing how we understand cosmic history.
articles.summary: Dark energy, the mysterious force driving cosmic expansion, may have reversed from negative to positive approximately 9.5 billion years ago. This discovery could fundamentally reshape our understanding of the universe's evolution and ultimate fate.

articles.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
articles.description: Earth's water may have been born in the planet's fiery atmosphere rather than delivered by icy comets or asteroids. Scientists discovered that rocky pebbles reacting with hydrogen under extreme heat can produce water in minutes, potentially generating hundreds of oceans' worth during Earth's formation. The findings suggest that water may be a natural part of how rocky planets form, rather than something that must arrive from space.
articles.summary: New research suggests Earth's water may have originated in our planet's early atmosphere rather than being delivered by comets or asteroids. This finding reveals a remarkable chapter in how our life-sustaining oceans were formed.

articles.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields
articles.description: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has revealed a surprising secret hidden within the chaos of space: turbulent magnetic fields reverse their direction of rotation when examined at extremely small scales. The discovery exposes an unexpected pattern in solar wind turbulence that could help scientists better understand solar activity and predict geomagnetic storms.
articles.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe has uncovered hidden patterns within the Sun's turbulent magnetic fields, revealing surprising order in apparent chaos. This discovery advances our understanding of solar dynamics and space weather.

articles.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
articles.description: SpaceX's Starship megarocket reached orbit today (Nov. 13) during its 15th test flight, but the company scrapped a plan to catch the vehicle's massive booster back at the launch site.
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship megarocket achieved orbit during its 15th test flight on November 13, demonstrating continued progress toward operational capability. The ambitious test advances the development of humanity's most powerful launch system.

articles.title: Scientists discover mysterious radio signals coming every eight minutes from deep space
articles.description: Astronomers in have linked the regular radio pulses to an unusual pairing of celestial bodies 5,000 light-years from Earth.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified mysterious radio signals repeating every eight minutes from deep space 5,000 light-years away, linking them to an unusual celestial pair.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA has opened applications for astronauts who will live and work on the Moon as part of its lunar exploration program.

articles.title: La sonde européenne Hera vient de photographier cet astéroïde à près de 60 km de distance : un cliché époustouflant
articles.description: Quatre ans après que la NASA a volontairement écrasé un engin sur un astéroïde, nous avons enfin une vue en gros plan des dégâts !
articles.summary: The European space probe Hera has captured stunning close-up images of an asteroid from 60 kilometers away, four years after NASA's successful impact mission.

articles.title: Zum ersten Mal in der Geschichte baut Roboter eigenständig eine Struktur im Weltraum zusammen
articles.description: Ohne Menschen vor Ort hat ein Roboter im All autonom ein Bauteil errichtet. Es könnte der Anfang roboterbasierten Baus im Orbit sein.
articles.summary: A robot has autonomously assembled a structure in space for the first time, marking a historic milestone in robotic space construction. This breakthrough could herald the beginning of robot-based construction in orbital environments.

articles.title: Blue Origin Unveils Their Northstar Engine! - Weekly Spaceflight News [6:22]
articles.description: In this week's Avid Space Industry Update Blue Origin announces multiple new technologies in the works, astronauts perform another successful spacewalk at the ISS and a new heavy-lift rocket is announced. Blue Origin Unveils Their Northstar Engine! - Weekly S…
articles.summary: Blue Origin reveals multiple new engine technologies including the Northstar engine in this week's spaceflight industry update. The announcement signals major advances in commercial spaceflight propulsion systems.

articles.title: NASA Just Made a Bunch of Moon Base Announcements: Here’s What They Are
articles.description: NASA just wrapped up its Max Power event, the agency’s first-ever aerospace technology expo that took place Wednesday through Sunday at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Featuring discussions, panels, announcements and technology demonstrations, the bigges…
articles.summary: NASA announced multiple lunar base initiatives at its inaugural Max Power aerospace technology expo. These announcements represent significant progress toward sustainable human presence on the Moon.

articles.title: A radical theory says the universe is twice as old as we thought
articles.description: A provocative new cosmological model suggests the Universe could be 26.7 billion years old and might not need dark matter or dark energy to explain its behavior. University of Ottawa researchers tested the theory against several major astronomical observation…
articles.summary: A bold new cosmological model proposes the universe could be 26.7 billion years old and potentially eliminate the need for dark matter. This provocative theory opens exciting new avenues for understanding cosmic history.

articles.title: A mysterious 93-billion-mile cosmic structure may be the wreckage of colliding worlds
articles.description: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has revealed surprising new details about a mysterious, 93-billion-mile-long cloud of dark, fluffy dust that may have formed when massive planetary bodies collided. The discovery challenges previous assumptions about the str…
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has revealed new details about a mysterious 93-billion-mile cosmic structure that may represent the remnants of colliding worlds. This discovery provides insights into planetary system formation and evolution.

articles.title: Shape-Shifting Robotic "Slugs" Could One Day Crawl Across Alien Worlds
articles.description: Robots have been a mainstay of our early space exploration efforts. But they normally have wheels. Or in some cases, rotors. While those solutions are great on flat ground, they struggle with jagged boulders or tight crevices. So engineers have been working on alternative robotic form factors, and a recent paper in Nature Machine Intelligence from researchers at Colorado State University’s Adaptive Robotics Lab, describes a unique morphology using a design principle typically seen in architecture rather than robotics - tensegrity.
articles.summary: Scientists are developing shape-shifting robotic slugs that could traverse challenging terrain on alien worlds, expanding the possibilities for future space exploration rovers.

articles.title: A Brief-ish History of METI. Part III: The Legacy of Frank Drake & Carl Sagan
articles.description: Carl Sagan and Frank Drake were pivotal to the development of the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI) and Messaging Extraterrestrial Intelligence (METI), as exemplified by the Pioneer Plaques and Voyager Golden Records.
articles.summary: A historical examination of Frank Drake and Carl Sagan's foundational contributions to SETI and METI, celebrating their visionary work in seeking extraterrestrial intelligence.

articles.title: Gemini and DECam showcase a young Type Ia supernova
articles.description: A star's explosive demise has added a shiny new feature to NGC 1433, a barred spiral galaxy approximately 50 million light-years away in the southern constellation Horologium (the Pendulum Clock). New images of supernova SN 2026ahvu from the U.S. Department of Energy–fabricated Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and the Gemini South telescope capture the explosion against its galactic surroundings, recording an event that is changing in appearance from night to night.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Gemini and DECam observatories captured images of a young Type Ia supernova in the galaxy NGC 1433, providing fresh insights into stellar explosions and cosmic distance measurements.

articles.title: Automated assembly in space is the future and NOM4D is showing the way
articles.description: If we want big things in space, we'll have to build and assemble them there. Rocket fairings are not large enough to accommodate the large things we want to have in space. Not only that, but the stubborn rocket equation refuses to bend itself to our desires.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NOM4D demonstrates automated assembly technologies in space, showcasing the future capability to construct large structures and infrastructure beyond Earth's limitations.

articles.title: Hubble offers cosmic sampler of targets for Roman
articles.description: A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA's Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has cataloged diverse gravitational lenses that will serve as valuable targets for the upcoming Roman Space Telescope mission.
